question.:question/problem: Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨3\left(u\right),\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,v\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(3\left(u\right)),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v\operatorname{cos}⁡u)⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,-v\operatorname{sin}⁡u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(3\left(u\right)),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v\operatorname{cos}⁡u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 3\left(1\right) & \operatorname{sin}⁡v & -v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 0 & u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & \operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}\operatorname{sin}⁡v & -v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & \operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}3\left(1\right) & -v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}3\left(1\right) & \operatorname{sin}⁡v \\ 0 & u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v+uv\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,- 3 \cos{(u )},\,3 u \cos{(v )}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}+1),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(3\left({v}^{3}+1\right)),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4\left(2u+v\right))⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,8⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(3\left({v}^{3}+1\right)),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4\left(2u+v\right))⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,9 v^{2},\,4⟩\end{aligned}

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2 u + 2 v,\,3 v^{2} + 3 \sin{(u )},\,u v⟩.

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2 u + 2 v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(3 v^{2} + 3 \sin{(u )}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,3 \cos{(u )},\,v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2 u + 2 v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(3 v^{2} + 3 \sin{(u )}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,6 v,\,u⟩\end{aligned}

$$

$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=3\left({u}^{2}+1\right),\,y=4\left({v}^{3}+1\right),\,z=2\left(2u+v\right).
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨3\left({u}^{2}+1\right),\,4\left({v}^{3}+1\right),\,2\left(2u+v\right)⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(3\left({u}^{2}+1\right)),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4\left({v}^{3}+1\right)),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2\left(2u+v\right))⟩ \\  & =⟨6 u,\,0,\,4⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(3\left({u}^{2}\right)),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4\left({v}^{3}+1\right)),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2\left(2u+v\right))⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,12 v^{2},\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 3\left(2u\right) & 0 & 2\left(2\right) \\ 0 & 4\left(3{v}^{2}\right) & 2\left(1\right)\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}0 & 2\left(2\right) \\ 4\left(3{v}^{2}\right) & 2\left(1\right)\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}3\left(2u\right) & 2\left(2\right) \\ 0 & 2\left(1\right)\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}3\left(2u\right) & 0 \\ 0 & 4\left(3{v}^{2}\right)\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨- 48 v^{2},\,- 12 u,\,72 u v^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
